- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; reduce subsequent forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 1–2% for next 2–3 periods.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to recent sentiment swings; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values if sentiment volatility > 0.5.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +0.67), model often misreads trend; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days for adjustment.
